title: CUDA caching allocator: separate env keys, private pools and stream aliasing
summary: PyTorch v2.15 parses CUDA allocator settings once, routes some allocations into private pools without starting capture, and aliases low-priority streams after 32 distinct requests.

hardware: CUDA devices using the pinned PyTorch caching allocator
software: pytorch/pytorch at 31a77fc9c0a7c6fff15a1ff58c743f53b1a9d457; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Question is device allocator or CUDA stream-pool behavior, not the v2.8 host-copy owner

claims.description: CUDAAllocatorConfig reads PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF, then PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF on ROCm, then PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF, in a once-initialized static instance.
beginAllocateToPool can run without cudaStreamBeginCapture. markCaptureBegin is a separate notification. Low-priority CUDA streams are a 32-wide round-robin pool.

downstream_impact: vLLM CUDA graphs: a private mempool is not evidence that capture has started.
Host pinned-memory reuse stays on the v2.8 host-memory-management owner; this card does not replace it.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream performance result.
validation_plan: Under a later authorized run, record the env before process start, compare pool id with and without capture, and check whether the 33rd low-priority stream aliases the first.
limitations: CUDACachingAllocator.cpp and AcceleratorAllocatorConfig bodies were not read, so deprecated max_split_size numbers are not restated.
No local allocator or latency measurement. Imported and locally unverified.
